correctness.rationale: For n,m>=2, diagonal normalization gives T_nm=sqrt(m/n)/[(n+m+1)log m]. Relative to L_nm=1_{m>n}/sqrt(nm)log m, the two exact difference formulas have column squared sums bounded by C/[m(log m)^2]; thus T-L is Hilbert–Schmidt. With h_n=log(1+1/n), phi_n=h_n^(-1/2)1_[log n,log(n+1)), J embeds l2 into L2([log 2,infinity)), and A f(s)=int_s^infty f(t)/t dt: off-diagonal rectangle oscillations, diagonal area bounds and summable errors show L-J*AJ and A-PAP are Hilbert–Schmidt, so A-JTJ* is HS. The unitary log(s) plus s^(1/2) change converts A to one-sided exponential convolution B with L1 kernel mass 2; broad weakly-null packets attain essential norm 2. For lambda!=0 the first-order resolvent equation u'+(lambda^{-1}-1/2)u=h/lambda gives Fredholm index 1 inside |lambda-1|<1 and 0 outside, with Weyl packets on the circle. At lambda=0, original T has weakly null columns with squared norms O((m log m)^(-1)), ensuring non-Fredholm independent of the zero extension. The original two-space map has no intrinsic Fredholm spectrum. Analytic estimates, not finite truncation, establish infinite-dimensional statements.
